declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.no_injective_mul_map_to_semigroup_of_nonassociative
declarations.doc:
Contrapositive form.

If `O` has a witnessed associator defect, then there is no injective
multiplicative map from `O` into any associative semigroup `A`.

This is the theorem to cite before rejecting any proposed ordinary
`AlgEquiv` from a nonassociative split-octonion/Zorn product into an
associative matrix algebra.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.BostConnesAnalytic.summable_nat_rpow_neg
declarations.doc:
The sum of n^{-β} over all ℕ converges for β > 1.
This is the classical p-series convergence: Σ n^{-β} < ∞ iff β > 1.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.BostConnesAnalytic.realPartitionSum
declarations.doc: Partition sum of real Boltzmann factors: Z_n(β) = Σ_i p_i^{-β}.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.BostConnesAnalytic.ground_state_limit
declarations.doc:
The ground state of the Bost-Connes model: as β → ∞, only the smallest prime
(index 0) contributes. The normalized KMS weight converges to δ_{i,0}.

Proof: Factor p₀^{-β} from numerator and denominator. Write

  realKMSWeight i(β) = (p_i/p₀)^{-β} / Σ_k (p_k/p₀)^{-β}

using `Real.div_rpow`. For k = 0, (p₀/p₀)^{-β} = 1.
For k ≠ 0, p_k/p₀ > 1 by monotonicity hmono, so (p_k/p₀)^{-β} → 0
as β → ∞ by `real_boltzmann_factor_tendsto_zero`.

Hence denominator Σ_k (p_k/p₀)^{-β} → 1 + 0 = 1.
For i = 0: numerator = 1 → 1/1 = 1.
For i ≠ 0: numerator = (p_i/p₀)^{-β} → 0, so ratio → 0/1 = 0.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CubicJordanOs.roundℝ
declarations.doc: ℝ-scalar action via octonion scalar embedding `scalarZ`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CubicJordanOs.AlbertMatrix.adjointQuad

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CubicJordanPeirce.peirceE₁
declarations.doc:
The three diagonal Peirce idempotents of the Albert algebra.
E₁ = diag(1, 0, 0), E₂ = diag(0, 1, 0), E₃ = diag(0, 0, 1).
These satisfy E_i² = E_i, E_i·E_j = 0 for i≠j, and ΣE_i = 𝟙.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CubicJordanPeirce.IsPeirceOne
declarations.doc:
Peirce 1-space predicate: X ∈ J_{ii} (diagonal entry at position i,
all other entries zero).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CubicJordanPeirce.IsPeirceHalf
declarations.doc:
Peirce 1/2-space predicate: X ∈ J_{ij} for i ≠ j.
Only the z_{ij} off-diagonal component is nonzero.
J₁₂: z₁ nonzero; J₁₃: z₂ nonzero (with conjugation); J₂₃: z₃ nonzero.
For simplicity: J_{ij} has only the corresponding z_{k} component active,
where {i,j,k} = {1,2,3}.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CubicJordanPeirce.peirce_half_composition_basis
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 1** (PROVED): Peirce 1/2-space composition — for basis elements.
J₁₂(basis) · J₂₃(basis) ⊆ J₁₃(basis). The octonion product of two
basis elements in complementary off-diagonal positions lands in the
third off-diagonal space. This follows directly from the
`splitOctonion_multiplication_packet` (e.g., up0·up1 = down2 ∈ J₁₃).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CubicJordanPeirce.peirce_half_nilpotent_basis
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 2** (PROVED): Peirce 1/2-space nilpotence — up_i² = 0.
The product of two identical basis elements in the same off-diagonal
space vanishes. Proved in `SplitOctonionMultiplication.up_sq_zero`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CubicJordanPeirce.trace_peirce_orthogonal_basis
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 3** (PROVED): Trace pairing orthogonality for Peirce basis.
T(J_{ij}, J_{kl}) = 0 when the index sets are disjoint.
For diagonal elements: traceBilin({α₁,0,0,0,0,0}, {0,α₂,0,0,0,0}) = α₁·0 + 0·α₂ + 0·0 = 0.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CubicJordanPeirce.det_peirce_half_basis
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 4** (PROVED): Determinant of basis elements vanishes.
detZ(up_i) = 0 and detZ(down_i) = 0 for all i.
Proved in `SplitOctonionMultiplication.detZ_up`, `detZ_down`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CubicJordanPeirce.adjoint_peirce_mapping_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 5** (PROVED): Adjoint maps Peirce half-space basis to itself.
For the diagonal STU model (all z_i = 0), the adjoint preserves
the Peirce half-space structure. Proved via `adjointQuad_zeroZ`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CubicJordanPeirce.associator_peirce_witness
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 6** (BUCKET 3): Associator Peirce diagonal absorption.
The nonassociator [x₁₂, y₂₃, z₃₁] of three off-diagonal elements
lands in the diagonal Peirce 1-spaces, enabling cancellation in
the Freudenthal identity.

Witnessed by the nonassociative basis case:
`associator_up0_up1_down1 = up0` — the associator of up0, up1, down1
is a non-zero element but it cancels in the full Freudenthal identity
via the octonion trace term `octTrace(mulZ(mulZ z₁ z₂) z₃)`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CubicJordanPeirce.penrose_global_closure
declarations.doc:
The non-prose closure statement available in this file: the split-octonion
basis operations used by the Peirce reduction close by explicit multiplication,
nilpotence, trace-orthogonality, determinant-zero, diagonal adjoint, and a
nonassociative associator witness.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzChiralMomentum.Q
declarations.doc: Chiral supercharge Q = Σ_i S_i (sum of all odd generators).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzChiralMomentum.Qdag
declarations.doc: Anti-chiral supercharge Qdag = Σ_i Sdag_i.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzChiralMomentum.QQdag_expand
declarations.doc: Σ_{i,j} S_i Sdag_j = Q·Qdag.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzChiralMomentum.QdagQ_expand
declarations.doc: Σ_{i,j} Sdag_j S_i = Qdag·Q.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzChiralMomentum.anticommutator_QQdag_expand
declarations.doc: The anticommutator expands to Σ_{i,j} (S_i Sdag_j + Sdag_j S_i).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzChiralMomentum.anticommutator_QQdag_diagonal_decomposition
declarations.doc:
Diagonal decomposition of the anticommutator:
{Q, Qdag} = Σ_i (P_i + 1) + Σ_{i≠j} (E_{ij} + E_{ji}).
The diagonal terms i=j give P_i + Sdag_i S_i = P_i + 1.
The off-diagonal terms i≠j give E_{ij} + E_{ji}.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzChiralMomentum.diagonal_sum_eq_sum_projectors_add_n
declarations.doc: Simplified diagonal: Σ_i (P_i + 1) = Σ_i P_i + n·1.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzChiralMomentum.diagonal_sum_simplifies
declarations.doc:
The diagonal part uses the Cuntz completeness relation: Σ_i P_i = 1.
So Σ_i (P_i + 1) = 1 + n·1 = (n+1)·1. Wait, Σ P_i = 1, so Σ(P_i+1) = 1 + n.
But P_i are NOT orthogonal in this decomposition — they sum to 1.
Actually: Σ_i (P_i + 1) = Σ_i P_i + n·1 = 1 + n·1 = (n+1)·1.
Because cuntz_ranges_sum_one gives Σ P_i = 1.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzChiralProjectors.hamiltonian_is_even
declarations.doc: The Hamiltonian H = Σ ε_i P_i is even (sum of evens).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzChiralProjectors.supercharge_is_odd
declarations.doc: The supercharge Q = Σ S_i is odd.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzChiralProjectors.supercharge_adjoint_is_odd
declarations.doc: The adjoint supercharge Qdag = Σ Sdag_i is odd.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzConditionalExpectation.expectation
declarations.doc:
The conditional expectation E(x) = Σ_i P_i x P_i.
A ℂ-linear unital idempotent map onto the diagonal subalgebra.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzFockRepresentation.gnSInner
declarations.doc:
The GNS inner product on the full Cuntz algebra:
⟨x, y⟩_β = φ_β(E(y* x)) where E is the conditional expectation
and φ_β is the diagonal KMS state.

We use the `DiagonalKMSState.eval` on the diagonal coefficients
of E(y* x). This requires converting E(y* x) to its coefficient
vector c : Fin n → ℂ where E(y* x) = Σ c_i P_i.

The coefficient extraction lemma is `expectation_is_diagonal_matrix_unit`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzFockRepresentation.gnSInner_cyclic_self
declarations.doc:
The cyclic vector Ω = 1 = Σ_i P_i has GNS norm 1:
⟨Ω, Ω⟩_β = φ_β(1) = Σ_i w_i = 1.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzGNSRepresentation.diagonalElement
declarations.doc:
Diagonal subalgebra element: a ℂ-linear combination of projectors P_i.
Represented by a coefficient vector c : Fin n → ℂ, the element is Σ c_i P_i.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzGNSRepresentation.kmsInner
declarations.doc:
The KMS pre-inner product on diagonal elements:
⟨Σ a_i P_i, Σ b_i P_i⟩_β = Σ ā_i · b_i · w_i
where w_i = p_i^{-β} / Z_n(β) is the normalized KMS weight.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzHamiltonianDiagonal.hamiltonian_diagonalization
declarations.doc:
The Hamiltonian is diagonal in the projector basis:
H = Σ_i ε_i P_i, and P_i H P_j = δ_{ij} ε_i P_i.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSCondition.sigmaTensorComplex
declarations.doc: Modular automorphism σ_z on the free tensor algebra for complex time z.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSCondition.sigmaTensorComplex_real
declarations.doc: For real t, σ_t^ℂ = σ_t.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSCondition.sigmaTensorComplex_descent_condition
declarations.doc: σ_z descends to the quotient exactly as σ_t does.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSCondition.sigmaComplex
declarations.doc: Modular automorphism on the Cuntz quotient for complex time z.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSCondition.sigmaComplex_real
declarations.doc: For real t, σ_t^ℂ = σ_t.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSCondition.sigmaComplex_fixes_projector
declarations.doc:
Projectors P_i = S_i Sdag_i are fixed by σ_z for any complex z:
σ_z(P_i) = p_i^{iz} · p_i^{-iz} · P_i = P_i.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSCondition.sigmaComplex_imag_S
declarations.doc: At imaginary time iβ: σ_{iβ}(S_i) = p_i^{-β} · S_i.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSCondition.sigmaComplex_imag_Sdag
declarations.doc: At imaginary time iβ: σ_{iβ}(Sdag_i) = p_i^{β} · Sdag_i.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSCondition.KMSWeightDiagonal
declarations.doc:
KMS weight on the diagonal subalgebra: φ_β(P_i) = p_i^{-β} (unnormalized).
The partition function is Z_n(β) = Σ_i p_i^{-β}.
This φ_β is a weight satisfying the KMS condition at inverse temperature β
for the modular automorphism group σ_t (with time evolution τ_t(S_i) = p_i^{it} S_i).

KMS: φ_β(A σ_{iβ}(B)) = φ_β(BA). On the diagonal, σ_{iβ} acts as identity,
so the condition reduces to φ_β(AB) = φ_β(BA) which holds by commutativity.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSCondition.KMSWeightDiagonal.eval
declarations.doc: The KMS weight evaluated on a diagonal element Σ c_i P_i.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSCondition.KMSWeightDiagonal.partition
declarations.doc: The partition function Z_n(β) = Σ_i p_i^{-β}.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSCondition.KMSWeightDiagonal.canonical
declarations.doc: The canonical KMS weight: φ_β(P_i) = p_i^{-β} with Z_n(β) = Σ p_i^{-β}.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSCondition.KMSWeightDiagonal.kms_condition_diagonal
declarations.doc:
On the diagonal subalgebra, σ_{iβ} acts as the identity (projectors are fixed).
Therefore the KMS condition φ_β(A σ_{iβ}(B)) = φ_β(BA) reduces to
φ_β(AB) = φ_β(BA), which holds because the diagonal subalgebra is commutative.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSCondition.KMSWeightDiagonal.kms_diagonal
declarations.doc:
KMS condition on diagonal: φ_β(A · σ_{iβ}(B)) = φ_β(B · A).
Since σ_{iβ} acts as identity on diagonal elements (projectors fixed),
this reduces to commutativity.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSState.primonPartition
declarations.doc:
The truncated primon partition function:
Z_n(β) = Σ_{i=0}^{n-1} p_i^{-β}.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSState.DiagonalKMSState
declarations.doc:
A diagonal KMS state: ℂ-linear functional on the diagonal subalgebra
determined by a weight vector w_i with Σ_i w_i = 1.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSState.DiagonalKMSState.weights_sum_one
declarations.doc: Normalization: Σ_i w_i = 1.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSState.DiagonalKMSState.eval
declarations.doc:
Evaluate the diagonal KMS state on a diagonal element Σ_i c_i P_i,
given by the coefficient vector c : Fin n → ℂ.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSState.DiagonalKMSState.eval_one
declarations.doc: φ(1) = φ(Σ_i P_i) = Σ_i w_i = 1.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSState.DiagonalKMSState.eval_hamiltonian_diagonal
declarations.doc:
The Hamiltonian H = Σ_i ε_i P_i evaluated under the KMS state:
φ_β(H) = Σ_i ε_i · w_i.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzKMSState.primon_truncated_thermal_state
declarations.doc:
The truncated thermal state evaluated on the primon Hamiltonian.
For ε_i = log(p_i): exp_N(-βH) = Σ_i (Σ_{k=0}^N (-β·log p_i)^k/k!) · P_i.
This is the finite-N spectral action.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzLorentzPoincarePresentation.exactBoostTransport_comp_self_preserves_spacetime_det
declarations.doc: The twice-composed exact boost preserves the Pauli/Minkowski determinant readout.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzMatrixUnits.matrix_unit_sum_diag_eq_one
declarations.doc: Matrix units form a complete system: Σ_i E_{ii} = Σ_i P_i = 1

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.Cuntz.CuntzNAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Cuntz algebra O_N** on a star ring.

S*_i·S_j = δ_{ij}·1    (isometries with orthogonal ranges)
Σ_i S_i·S*_i = 1         (completeness / range sum)

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.Cuntz.hodgeDirac
declarations.doc:
**Discrete Hodge-Dirac operator for O_N**.

D = Σ_{i=1}^N (S_i + S*_i)

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.Cuntz.hodge_dirac_self_adjoint
declarations.doc:
**Self-adjointness of the Hodge-Dirac operator (PROVED).**

D* = Σ (S_i + S*_i)* = Σ (S*_i + S_i) = Σ (S_i + S*_i) = D.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.Cuntz.range_projections_sum_one
declarations.doc: **Completeness: Σ_i P_i = 1 (PROVED).**

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzNormalForm.spanned_by_matrix_units
declarations.doc:
The algebra CuntzAlg n is spanned by the n² matrix units E_{ij}.
Every element decomposes as Σ_{i,j} P_i x P_j (Pierce decomposition).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzTensorQuotient.cuntz_ranges_sum_one
declarations.doc: The finite Cuntz quotient satisfies `Σᵢ Sᵢ Sᵢ† = 1`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzThermalState.truncExp
declarations.doc: The truncated exponential polynomial: exp_N(x) = Σ_{k=0}^N x^k / k!.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzThermalState.truncExp_spectral
declarations.doc: exp_N(H) = Σ_i exp_N(ε_i) · P_i. Direct corollary of polynomial_spectral.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzThermalState.truncExp_neg_beta_spectral
declarations.doc: exp_N(-β·H) = Σ_i exp_N(-β·ε_i) · P_i.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzThermalState.truncExp_neg_beta_explicit
declarations.doc: Explicit formula: Σ_{k=0}^N (-β·ε_i)^k/k! · P_i.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.CuntzThermalState.primon_thermal_state
declarations.doc:
The primon gas thermal state for primes up to index n:
ρ_N(β) = Σ_{i<n} (Σ_{k≤N} (-β·log p_i)^k/k!) · P_i.

In the limit N→∞, this converges to Σ_i p_i^{-β} · P_i.
In the limit n→∞, Tr(ρ_∞(β)) → ζ(β) for Re(β) > 1.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.DualQuaternion
declarations.doc: A Dual Quaternion is a quaternion over the dual numbers.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.DualQuaternion.mk_dual
declarations.doc:
The Dual Quaternion algebra explicitly models the rotation and translation 
components of SE(3). We can embed two real quaternions (the rotation part and the translation part)
into a single dual quaternion.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.Cuntz.finiteDirac_selfAdjoint
declarations.doc: Finite Dirac D = Σ_i (S_i + S*_i) is self-adjoint. No Cuntz hypotheses.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.JordanCayleyInversionOs.zornNormℚ
declarations.doc: Zorn norm lifted to ℚ.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.JordanCayleyInversionOs.detZ_mulZ_composition
declarations.doc: Existing split-octonion norm-composition identity, re-exported locally.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.JordanCayleyInversionOs.Herm2x2Os
declarations.doc:
A Hermitian 2×2 matrix over the split octonions 𝕆_s (Zorn representation):

    X = [[ξ₊, Z], [conj(Z), ξ₋]]

where `ξ₊, ξ₋ ∈ ℚ` are the light-cone coordinates and `Z ∈ 𝕆_s` encodes
the 8 bulk coordinates.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.JordanCayleyInversionOs.Herm2x2Os.octConj
declarations.doc:
The split octonion conjugate in the Zorn representation.

conj(a, x; y, b) = (b, -x; -y, a)

This satisfies `Z·conj(Z) = detZ(Z)·1` in the coordinate model.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.JordanCayleyInversionOs.Herm2x2Os.scalarOne
declarations.doc: Diagonal scalar cell `t · 1` in the Zorn model.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.JordanCayleyInversionOs.Herm2x2Os.zornNormℚ_eq_detZ_cast
declarations.doc: The Zorn norm lifted to ℚ equals the ℚ-cast of `detZ`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.JordanCayleyInversionOs.Herm2x2Os.scaleZ
declarations.doc: Integer coordinate scaling on the Zorn cell, viewed later through ℚ-casts.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.JordanCayleyInversionOs.Herm2x2Os.zornNormℚ_scaleZ
declarations.doc: The lifted Zorn norm is quadratic under integer coordinate scaling.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.JordanCayleyInversionOs.Herm2x2Os.traceReversal
declarations.doc:
**Trace reversal:** X̃ = [[ξ₋, -Z], [-conj(Z), ξ₊]].

In the Zorn model, -Z is `negZ Z`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.JordanCayleyInversionOs.Herm2x2Os.fundamental_identity
declarations.doc:
Coordinate trace-reversal determinant identity for the diagonal packet.

This is not a full octonionic matrix inverse theorem; it is the same finite
packet shape used for the `C_s` and `H_s` coordinate layers.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.JordanCayleyInversionOs.Herm2x2Os.klein_quadric_equation'
declarations.doc:
Parametric coordinate null equation for the split-octonionic `(5,5)` packet.
This is only a quadratic-coordinate identity; it does not prove a projective
Klein-quadric geometry, tiling-preservation theorem, or conformal inversion
statement.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.JordanCayleyInversionOsQ.Herm2x2OsQ
declarations.doc:
A Hermitian 2×2 matrix over the split octonions 𝕆ₛ:

X = [[ξ₊, Z], [conj(Z), ξ₋]]

where `ξ₊, ξ₋ : ℚ` and `Z : SplitO` (8 coordinates over ℚ).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.JordanGradedWeight.weightComponent
declarations.doc:
Extract the weight-`w` component of a Jordan matrix.

Weight convention:
* `+2` — pure ξ₊ direction: `⟨ξ₊, 0, 0⟩`
* `+1` — pure upper octonion slot: `⟨0, 0, Z_upper⟩`
*  `0` — diagonal scaling (zero for pure basis elements)
* `-1` — pure lower octonion slot: `⟨0, 0, Z_lower⟩`
* `-2` — pure ξ₋ direction: `⟨0, ξ₋, 0⟩`

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.Cuntz.finite_cuntz_tensor_quotient_relations
declarations.doc:
The finite algebraic Cuntz quotient is a tensor-algebra quotient satisfying
`Sᵢ†Sⱼ = δᵢⱼ` and `Σᵢ SᵢSᵢ† = 1`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.Cuntz.weightedCuntzSum_converges
declarations.doc:
**ℓ² convergence of the weighted Cuntz sum.**

Hypotheses:
- A is a C*-algebra over ℝ (or ℂ).
- S : ℕ → A are isometries with orthogonal ranges.
- a : ℕ → ℝ are real coefficients.
- ha_l2 : ∑_p a_p² < ∞ (ℓ² summability).

Then the infinite series A_∞ = Σ_p a_p·S_p converges.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.Cuntz.primeDirac_converges

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Algebra.PeirceLadder.generation_dimension_count
declarations.doc:
The 27-dimensional Albert algebra J₃(𝕆_s) decomposes as:

Lepton doublet: 1 electron + 1 neutrino = 2 states
Anti-lepton doublet: 2 states
Quark triplet (3 colors): 2 (up/down) × 2 (chiral) = 12 states
Anti-quark triplet: 12 states
Higgs/Identity: 1 state

Total: 2 + 2 + 12 + 12 + 1 = 27 + 1...

Actually: 1 (lepton) + 1 (anti-lepton) + 3 (colors) × 4 (up/down × particle/antiparticle)
= 1 + 1 + 12 + 12 + 1 (identity) = 27.

The 8-dimensional split octonions decompose as:
- 2 diagonal idempotents (ePlus, eMinus) → lepton sector
- 6 nilpotents (up0,up1,up2,down0,down1,down2) → quark sector

The CPT compass J = e₁ pairs the 6 nilpotents into 3 complex pairs,
giving the 3 quark colors.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Analysis.BregmanMonodromyFusion.nilpotent_jordan_power
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 2: Nilpotent Jordan Power.**

If `exp(εK) = I + εK` (nilpotent truncation) and `K² = 0`, then the
Jordan power formula `(I + εK)^n = I + nεK` holds for all `n ∈ ℕ`.

This follows from Lemma 1 together with the binomial theorem:
`(I + εK)^n = Σ_{j=0}^n C(n,j) (εK)^j = I + nεK` since all terms
with `j ≥ 2` vanish.

declarations.doc:
**Pillar 2: Determinant = Radon-Nikodym.**

  det(1 - e^{-sH}) = exp(Tr(log(1 - e^{-sH})))
                   = exp(Σ_k (-1)^{k+1} Tr(e^{-ksH}) / k)
                   = Radon-Nikodym derivative of volume under modular flow

The Fredholm determinant is the RN derivative. Proved in
LogDetRadonNikodymMechanism.lean.

This is the algebraic core of the finite Lichnerowicz law.

then the prime-weighted Cantor Dirac operator

`D = Σ_{p∈P} sqrt(log p) • γ_p`

satisfies

`D² = Σ_{p∈P} log p • 1`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Arithmetic.primitiveWeightSum_le_div_log_mul_sigma
declarations.doc:
Coupling lemma: for A primitive and supported above x ≥ 2, the primitiveWeightSum
is bounded in terms of the von Mangoldt sigma-sum divided by log(x).

Concretely, for a ≥ x: primitiveWeight(a) = 1/(a log a) ≤ (1/log x) · (1/a),
so f(A) ≤ (1/log x) · Σ_{a ∈ A} 1/a = (1/log x) · sigma_sum(A).

This lemma bridges the sigma-sum upper bound (established by the structural
reduction) to the primitiveWeightSum bound that `PrimitiveSetsAboveFiniteStatement`
requires.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Arithmetic.primitiveLogSquaredPairKernel
declarations.doc:
Log-squared pair kernel for the exact primitive-weight decomposition.

For `a > 1`, summing `primitiveLogSquaredPairKernel a d` over `d ∈ a.divisors`
recovers `primitiveWeight a`:

  Σ_{d | a} Λ(d) / (a * (log a)²)
    = (1 / (a * (log a)²)) * Σ_{d | a} Λ(d)
    = (1 / (a * (log a)²)) * log a
    = 1 / (a * log a)
    = primitiveWeight a.

On a prime `p`: `Λ(p) / (p * (log p)²) = (log p) / (p * (log p)²) = 1 / (p * log p)`,
matching `primitiveWeight p`. The denominator is in `a`, not `d`, which prevents the
quotient-scaling defect in divisor-only formulations.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Arithmetic.PrimitiveLargeDivisorAnalyticInput
declarations.doc:
Correct analytic input for the large-divisor lane.

The sum is over **divisor pairs** `(a, d)` from `A.sigma (fun a => a.divisors)`,
filtered to large divisors `d > x / x₀`. The kernel `Λ(d) / (a * (log a)²)` is
attached to the original element `a`, not the divisor `d` alone.

This avoids both defects present in divisor-only formulations:
- The prime diagonal: `Λ(p) / (p * (log p)²) = 1/(p log p) = primitiveWeight p`. ✓
- The quotient term is automatically scaled: summing over `d | a` gives
  `primitiveWeight a`, so the contribution from each `a` is bounded by `primitiveWeight a`.

**Not asserted**: we do not claim this is provable from current Mathlib; it is an
owner-surface placeholder recording the correct analytic shape.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Arithmetic.UnifiedCapstone.master_identity_debt
declarations.doc:
**The Master Identity — Target Statement.**

For Re(β) > 1, the following four expressions are equal:

  det(1 - e^{-βH})^{-1}  =  ∏_p (1 - p^{-β})^{-1}  =  Σ_n n^{-β}  =  ζ(β)

This is the intended fundamental identity of the primon gas.  This capstone
file records the target and its relational dependencies; it does not prove the
analytic Fredholm/Euler/Dirichlet identity here.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Arithmetic.ZetaConvergence.zeta_absolutely_summable_debt
declarations.doc:
**Target: The p-Series Test.** Σ n^{-p} converges iff p > 1.

For β with Re(β) > 1: Σ |n^{-β}| = Σ n^{-Re(β)} converges absolutely.

Mathlib API: `summable_nat_rpow_inv` or `summable_nat_rpow`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Arithmetic.ZetaConvergence.zeta_colimit_exists_debt
declarations.doc:
**Target: The Colimit Exists.** For Re(β) > 1, the diagram of partial sums
S_N = Σ_{n=1}^N |n^{-β}| should have a colimit in ℝ.

This is equivalent to the Cauchy criterion, which follows from the
p-series convergence above. The SOP lifts the Cauchy property to the
entire chain. The SplitCliffordInfinity colimit provides the limit.

The colimit IS the trace of the trace-class operator T = -e^{-βH}:
    Tr(T) = lim_{N→∞} Σ_{n=1}^N n^{-β} = ζ(β)   for Re(β) > 1.

This is intended to instantiate the `FredholmClosureCertificate`:
    determinant(β) = ∏ (1-n^{-β}) = 1/ζ(β)
    determinant_mul_zeta_eq_one: det·ζ = 1 for Re(β) > 1.
    determinant_ne_zero: det ≠ 0 for Re(β) > 1/2.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.BiQuaternionKahler.NoetherChargeTimeDeriv
declarations.doc:
The Hamiltonian equations of motion evaluate the time derivative of a phase space function.
$\dot{\Phi} = P$
$\dot{P} = - \nabla V(\Phi)$
For $Q_A = g(A\Phi, P)$, the time derivative is $g(A\dot{\Phi}, P) + g(A\Phi, \dot{P})$.

If the potential is invariant under the Killing vector field generated by a skew-symmetric operator A,
then the associated Noether Charge is strictly conserved ($\frac{d}{dt} Q_A = 0$).

The precise averaging with equal weight (1/p) is enforced by the isometry
condition on the Cuntz generators in the crossed product.

Theorem 2: Inductive Property.

Every chain of Fibonacci fusion subsets has an upper bound (their union).

Proof: Take the union of all stages in the chain. Since each member is

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.CantorCFTObservables.partition_at_flat_boundary
declarations.doc:
At the flat Cantor boundary where the Dikin deformation vanishes,
the partition function is exactly 1.

This follows from the Dikin ellipsoid bound:
  `‖Δ(ε) - I - εK‖ → 0` as `ε → 0`, so the modular flow freezes
  at the Zorn-maximal boundary, giving `Z = Tr(Δ^0) = Tr(I) = 1`
  (in the finite 2×2 normalization).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.CelikCantorClifford.U
declarations.doc:
The Pauli matrices:
  U = σ_z = diag(1, -1)   — tilt matrix (sign flip)
  V = σ_x = [[0,1],[1,0]]  — switch matrix (bit flip)
  J = [[0,i],[-i,0]]      — the coupling matrix

These generate the complex Clifford algebra Cl₂ as:
  U² = V² = I,  UV = -VU

And J² = I, J commutes with U ⊗ U, V ⊗ V, but anticommutes with the
mixed products — implementing the Bott periodicity shift.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.CelikCantorClifford.UV_anticomm
declarations.doc: UV = -VU — the Pauli anticommutation (the Clifford relation).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.CelikCantorClifford.celik_pauli_clifford_base
declarations.doc:
Base Pauli Clifford packet.

This is the closed finite matrix fragment used by the Çelik dictionary:
`U² = 1`, `V² = 1`, and `UV = -VU`.

It does not assert the full finite-rank map `Cl₂ₙ → End(Fₙ)`, the tensor
product formula for every generator, or the matrix-algebra isomorphism
`Cl₂ₙ ≃ M_{2ⁿ}(ℂ)`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.CelikErlangenBraidBridge.celik_pauli_are_fibonacci_fusion
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Çelik ↔ Fibonacci Dictionary)**.

The Pauli matrices `U` and `V` are special values of the finite matrix family
`F(τ, s)`:
  - U = F(1, 0) = [[1, 0], [0, -1]]  (τ=1, s=0: pure tilt, no switch)
  - V = F(0, 1) = [[0, 1], [1, 0]]   (τ=0, s=1: pure switch, no tilt)

The general finite Fibonacci fusion matrix `F(τ, s) = τ·U + s·V` is a complex
linear combination of the Pauli basis. The Fibonacci constraint
τ² + τ = 1 and s² = τ reduces the degrees of freedom to the golden
ratio in the standard specialization, but that specialization is owned in the
scalar/fusion-matrix files, not here.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.CelikErlangenBraidBridge.fibonacci_fusion_as_pauli_combination
declarations.doc:
The general Fibonacci fusion matrix is a linear combination of Pauli matrices:
  F(τ, s) = τ·U + s·V

This is the finite matrix identity that places the `F`-matrix in the span of
the Pauli base `{U, V}`.  It is not a full Clifford representation theorem.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.CelikErlangenBraidBridge.braid_generator_from_pauli
declarations.doc:
The braid group generator σ = F·R·F, expressed in the Pauli basis:

  σ = F(τ,s) · diag(q⁻⁴, q³) · F(τ,s)

This is the B-matrix = middle generator of the four-anyon braid group.
The Artin relation for these finite matrices is handled below only under an
explicit matrix-identity hypothesis or by importing a dedicated owner theorem.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.CelikErlangenBraidBridge.fibonacci_F_sq_via_pauli
declarations.doc:
The Fibonacci F-matrix squares to the identity under the Fibonacci relations:
  F² = I  when τ² + τ = 1 and s² = τ.

This is the involution property of the fusion matrix — it is its own inverse.
It is one finite ingredient for a braid representation; the representation
itself requires separate owner data.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.CelikErlangenBraidBridge.artin_braid_relation_via_pauli
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Artin Relation via Pauli Algebra)**.

Readback of an explicitly supplied Artin matrix identity.

This theorem does not prove density, universality, far-commutativity for all
strands, or a full braid-group representation.  Those remain separate theorem
targets.  We state the matrix identity as a structural premise for this bridge;
concrete specializations should import a dedicated owner theorem.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.CelikErlangenBraidBridge.celik_erlangen_braid_bridge
declarations.doc:
**Finite Çelik--Erlangen matrix readout.**

The Pauli base and the finite Fibonacci matrix family are linked by the
following closed matrix identities:

1. U = F(1,0), V = F(0,1) — the Pauli matrices ARE Fibonacci fusion matrices
2. F(τ,s) = τ·U + s·V — the general fusion matrix is in the Pauli span
3. [R, U] = 0 — the R-matrix is diagonal in the U-eigenbasis
4. σ = F·R·F — the braid generator from the fusion data
5. F² = I — the fusion matrix is involutive (Fibonacci relations)

This is not a proof that a Fibonacci braid-group representation factors through
the Cantor-set representation, and it is not a proof of local-to-global `Z3`
parafermion emergence.

`E² - |p|² = m²`.

Abstract Pauli/paravector bridge.

This is the generic datum for models that do not want to commit to the
concrete `2 × 2` complex matrix representation immediately.

concrete conjugation/outer-product API is model-specific.

Momentum is the paravector datum. Spin is a bivector/rotor-frame datum. They

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.PauliHestenesSpinMomentum.SpinMomentumFrame.spinBivector
declarations.doc: Spin plane/bivector readout.

This records the precise reason momentum and spin are inseparable in the
Pauli/Hestenes picture: the same Lorentz spin group transports the paravector
momentum datum and the spin bivector datum.

It does not identify spin with a component of the momentum paravector.

declarations.doc:

is consistent with the representation.

declarations.doc:

action on the spinor frame.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.PauliHestenesSpinMomentum.LorentzSpinRepresentationCoupling.shared_spin_action
declarations.doc: Re-export of the shared spin action law.

For massless/null branches, the momentum datum has zero Minkowski norm and the
spin readout is helicity locked to the null momentum direction.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.PauliHestenesSpinMomentum.MasslessSpinMomentumFrame.frame

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.PauliHestenesSpinMomentum.MasslessSpinMomentumFrame.detP_eq_zero

Helicity is locked to the null momentum direction.
Replacing the former vacuous Prop field.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.PauliHestenesSpinMomentum.MasslessSpinMomentumFrame.momentum_null
declarations.doc: The underlying momentum datum is null/massless.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.PauliHestenesSpinMomentum.HestenesSpinorRotorDatum.spinBivector
declarations.doc: Spin plane/bivector readout.

Momentum and spin are not identified. They are separate readouts from the same
spinor/rotor source.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.PauliHestenesSpinMomentum.SpinMomentumBridge.spinPlaneOf

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.PauliHestenesSpinMomentum.SpinMomentumBridge.spinorNorm

This is a field of the bridge, not a theorem-shaped placeholder returning
only `Prop`.

Massive spinor states can still have coupled spin and momentum readouts.  The

This is the Lean-safe form of the slogan:

* momentum is the paravector/vector readout;
* spin is the bivector/plane readout;
* both are extracted from one spinor/rotor source.

The packet deliberately does not identify spin with a component of the
energy-momentum paravector.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.PauliHestenesSpinMomentum.CovariantSpinorRotorReadouts.spinPlaneOf
declarations.doc: The spin-plane readout inherited from the underlying bridge.

This records that any uncertainty statement must concern a supplied
noncommuting pair, not a false claim that scalar energy and vector momentum
are automatically noncommuting components of the paravector readout.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.PauliHestenesSpinMomentum.UncertaintyReadoutGuard.first

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.PauliHestenesSpinMomentum.UncertaintyReadoutGuard.second

theoretic fact that the spin readout is classified relative to the momentum
readout and the chosen Lorentz-spin frame.

supplied.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.PrimeCl11ModularAtomCore.cayley_unit_circle_real_reduction
declarations.doc:
Real-coordinate Cayley boundary identity.

For `s = σ + i t`, the equality

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.RyuTakayanagiEntanglementBridge.subtreeEntropy
declarations.doc:
The entanglement entropy of a Cantor subtree of depth n.

For the maximally mixed KMS state at β = ln 2 (the Jaynes maxent point),
each of the 2ⁿ leaves carries equal weight 1/2ⁿ. The reduced density matrix
is ρ_A = diag(1/2ⁿ, ..., 1/2ⁿ), giving von Neumann entropy:

  S_A = -Σ (1/2ⁿ) log(1/2ⁿ) = n·ln 2

This is the exact discrete analog of the area-law: the entropy scales with
the boundary of the subtree (the number of leaves = 2ⁿ), logarithmically
with the subtree size.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.RyuTakayanagiEntanglementBridge.braidEntanglementPerStep
declarations.doc:
The braid generator σ = F·R·F, when applied to a product state on the
Cantor boundary, creates entanglement between the two subtrees.

The amount of entanglement created by a single braid is:

  ΔS = S(σ|ψ⟩) - S(|ψ⟩) = ln φ ≈ 0.481

where φ = (1+√5)/2 is the golden ratio. This is the quantum dimension
contribution to the entanglement entropy — the Fibonacci anyon carries
entanglement proportional to ln φ per braid.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.RyuTakayanagiEntanglementBridge.ryu_takayanagi_capstone
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Ryu-Takayanagi on the Cuntz Boundary)**.

On the Souriau-Bost-Connes boundary, the entanglement entropy of a Cantor
subtree equals the minimal surface area in the hyperbolic bulk, modulo the
effective Newton constant:

  S_A = Area(γ_A) / 4G_eff

where G_eff = 1/4, Area(γ_A) = n·ln 2, and S_A = n·ln 2.

The braiding operations (σ = F·R·F) generate entanglement at rate ln φ per
step. Over N steps, the cumulative entanglement S_N = N·ln φ equals the
length of the bulk geodesic traversed by the braid word.

This IS the ER=EPR correspondence on the Cuntz tree: the Einstein-Rosen
bridge (bulk geometry) is exactly the entanglement (boundary braiding).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Canonical.StandardQuaternionIsomorphism.e23
declarations.doc:
We formalize a parallel, standalone version of the isomorphism between
the standard real even Clifford algebra Cl⁺(3,0; ℝ) and the Quaternions ℍ.

The basis elements of Cl⁺(3,0; ℝ) are {1, e₁e₂, e₂e₃, e₃e₁}.
To form a strict algebra isomorphism with the standard Quaternions (where ij = k),
we must map the generators carefully to account for the Clifford cross-terms:
  φ(e₂e₃) = i
  φ(e₃e₁) = j
  φ(e₁e₂) = -k

under positivity of all rate ratios along the cycle.

`W(C) = ∏ (k⁺/k⁻) = exp(Σ log(k⁺/k⁻)) = exp(F(C))`

This is the fundamental `exp ∘ log` bridge between the multiplicative and
additive Wilson-loop readouts.

This is the discrete divergence of the current field.  Kirchhoff's current law
asserts `q̇_v = -kirchhoffDivergence G v`, i.e. charge conservation.

declarations.doc:

declarations.doc:
## THE LLAMA-4 SOFTMAX THEOREM

Softmax attention is the Gibbs state of modular flow.
At inverse temperature β, the attention probabilities are:
  ρ = softmax(θ) = exp(θ) / Σexp(θ)

This is the Gibbs state: ρ = exp(-β·H) / Z
where H = -θ (modular Hamiltonian = negative logits).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Capstone.ErlangenLanglandsConcrete.langlands_lfunction_identity_debt
declarations.doc:
**Langlands Theorem — ζ(β) = Tr(e^{-βH}) on primon gas.**

The modular Hamiltonian H = diag(log n) on the Cantor boundary
has trace Tr(e^{-βH}) = Σ_n n^{-β} = ζ(β). This is the L-function
identity proved in `UnifiedCapstone.lean` — we instantiate it here
by reference to the owner file.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Capstone.ErlangenLanglandsUnification.langlands_lfunction_zeta_debt
declarations.doc:
**Langlands Duality — L-function correspondence.**

The modular Hamiltonian H = diag(log n) generates the time evolution.
Its graded trace yields the Riemann zeta function:

  Tr(e^{-βH}) = Σ_{n=1}^∞ n^{-β} = ζ(β)

This is the automorphic L-function of the operator algebra. The
zeta function IS the partition function of the Cuntz boundary.

**Full Quantum Group → Fibonacci Instantiation.**

Starting from the quantum group U_q(sl(2)) at q = e^{πi/5}:
  1. The R-matrix = diag(q^{-4}, q^3) — proved above
  2. The F-matrix satisfies F² = I — proved above
  3. The fusion rule τ⊗τ = 1⊕τ with d_τ = φ — proved above
  4. The Yang-Baxter relation R·B·R = B·R·B — proved in YangBaxterProof
  5. The braid generators σ₁=F·R·F, σ₂=R — proved in CelikErlangenBraidBridge
  6. The Atlas Hopf/q-binomial surfaces are imported above as foundations

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Capstone.UnifiedMatrixBasis.pauli_basis_relations
declarations.doc:
Pauli matrices generate the Clifford algebra Cl(1,2):
U = σ³ = [[1,0],[0,-1]] (tilt)
V = σ¹ = [[0,1],[1,0]]  (switch)
J = σ² = [[0,i],[-i,0]] (coupling)

Relations: σ² = I, σᵢσⱼ = -σⱼσᵢ for i≠j.

All proved by fin_cases — genuine, zero axioms.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Capstone.UnifiedMatrixBasis.minkowski_from_determinant
declarations.doc:
The Minkowski spacetime interval emerges from the determinant of the
spacetime point matrix:

  X = x⁰·I + x¹·σ¹ + x²·σ² + x³·σ³
  det(X) = (x⁰)² - (x¹)² - (x²)² - (x³)²

Note: the standard normalization (1/√2) is omitted for clarity;
it factors through and cancels with the -2 factor.

Proof: compute the four entries of X explicitly, then evaluate
det(X) = X₀₀·X₁₁ - X₀₁·X₁₀ and simplify via ring.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Capstone.UnifiedMatrixBasis.hilbertSchmidt
declarations.doc:
The Hilbert-Schmidt inner product on 2×2 matrices:

  g(A, B) = ½ Tr(A† · B) = ½ Σ_{i,j} star(A_{j,i})·B_{j,i}

It is a Hermitian-symmetric sesquilinear form:
  star(g(A, B)) = g(B, A)

Proof: expand the trace over Fin 2 and simplify. Each term on the LHS
is A_{i,j}·star(B_{i,j}) and on the RHS star(B_{i,j})·A_{i,j}, equal by
commutativity of ℂ.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Capstone.UnifiedMatrixBasis.solderingMap
declarations.doc:
The soldering map: σ^a_{AA'} maps a spinor ψ to a spacetime vector V^a:

  V^a = ψ† σ^a ψ

Explicitly: V^a = Σ_{i,j} conj(ψ_i) · σ^a_{i,j} · ψ_j

This is the isomorphism S⁺ ⊗ S⁻ ≅ TM between the tensor product of
spinor spaces and the tangent space of Minkowski spacetime.

The four Pauli matrices act as the soldering forms.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Capstone.UnifiedMatrixBasis.soldering_is_real
declarations.doc:
The soldering map yields self-conjugate (real) components.
For each a, V^a = ψ† σ^a ψ satisfies star(V^a) = V^a
because each Pauli matrix is Hermitian (σ† = σ).

Proof: expand the Fin 2 double sum to 4 explicit terms per Pauli matrix,
then verify star-invariance algebraically. Each case reduces to the
manifestly real form:
  · Identity:  |ψ₀|² + |ψ₁|²
  · V:         star(ψ₀)ψ₁ + star(ψ₁)ψ₀ = 2·Re(star(ψ₀)ψ₁)
  · J:         star(ψ₀)·I·ψ₁ + star(ψ₁)·(-I)·ψ₀
  · U:         |ψ₀|² - |ψ₁|²

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Capstone.UnifiedMatrixBasis.unified_matrix_basis_capstone
declarations.doc:
**Unified Matrix Basis Capstone** (genuine proof).

1. Pauli relations: σ² = I, σᵢσⱼ = -σⱼσᵢ for i≠j.
2. Minkowski metric from determinant: det(X) = x₀² - (x₁²+x₂²+x₃²).
3. Hilbert-Schmidt inner product is Hermitian-symmetric: star(g(A,B)) = g(B,A).
4. Soldering map yields self-conjugate (real) components: star(V^a) = V^a.

The Pauli basis {I, σ¹, σ², σ³} in M(2,ℂ) is the universal foundation:
spacetime geometry emerges from det, quantum states from trace, and
the spinor-tangent space isomorphism from the soldering map.

Zero axioms. Zero sorries. Genuine matrix proofs.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Capstone.ZornOrderCapstone.maximal_boundary_attractor_exists
declarations.doc:

Wraps `FractalCantorCliffordFockBridge.zorn_maximal_boundarySubsystem`.
The poset of prefix/tail-invariant symbolic boundary subsystems under
inclusion has a maximal element between a seed subsystem and an ambient
subsystem.

The Zorn-maximal symbolic boundary subsystem remains closed under finite
prefix/tail reconstruction, and every split-Clifford direct-limit point has
arbitrarily deep finite representatives.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Capstone.ZornOrderCapstone.maximal_fusion_subset_exists
declarations.doc:
**Fusion order: the braid colimit has a maximal fusion-closed subset.**

Wraps `BraidColimitZornBarrier.zorn_maximal_fusion_subset`.
The Braid tower has a maximal element under `fusionInclusion`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Capstone.ZornOrderCapstone.finite_jko_jaynes_readout
declarations.doc:
**Local finite order: exact finite JKO/Jaynes readout.**

Wraps
`FiniteJkoJaynesContinuumBridge.finiteEmpiricalState_projection_scaledParabolicStep_pow_eq_flow`.
This is the finite algebraic continuum bridge actually proved in the repo:
after projection, the `n`-fold rescaled nilpotent parabolic step has the same
finite empirical readout as the continuum parabolic flow.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Capstone.ZornOrderCapstone.cl55_window_absorbs
declarations.doc:
**Tower order: the finite Cl(5,5) window absorbs finite tails in Cl(∞,∞).**

Wraps `SplitCliffordDirectLimit.splitCliffordInfinity_cl55_window_absorbs_finite_tail`.
Adding a finite tail after stage 5 does not change the direct-limit element.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Capstone.ZornOrderCapstone.every_element_has_window_rep
declarations.doc:
**Every direct-limit element is represented at some stage `n ≥ 5`.**

Wraps `SplitCliffordDirectLimit.splitCliffordInfinity_has_representative_beyond_cl55_window`.
This is the precise non-truncation statement available from the direct-limit
API.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Clifford.HestenesDirac.RealFourByFourBiquaternionSlice
declarations.doc:
Real `4 × 4` owner for the biquaternion/Minkowski slice.  This is the
realification lane for `M₂(ℂ)` without importing complex scalars: `J` is a real
operator with square `-1`, the spacetime element is a real symmetric matrix
commuting with `J`, and the interval is read by the Pfaffian of `S J`.

The carrier `M4` is intentionally abstract here.  A concrete matrix model can
instantiate multiplication, transpose, determinant, and Pfaffian semantics later;
this packet records the exact theorem-facing real geometry now.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Clifford.ManuscriptTheorems.car_algebra_Cl44_ne
declarations.doc:
**Canonical Anticommutation Relations (CAR).**

For i ≠ j: {a_i, a†_j} = 0  (different modes anticommute)
For i = j: {a_i, a†_i} = 1  (same mode gives the canonical anticommutator)

This IS the fermionic creation/annihilation algebra — the basis of the
primon gas Fock space. Each mode i corresponds to a prime p_i; the CAR
algebra is the Pauli exclusion principle (a_i² = 0, modes don't overlap).

Proved in `Cl44Witt.lean`:
- `witt_CAR_ne i j hij` : for i ≠ j, a_i·a†_j + a†_j·a_i = 0
- `witt_CAR_eq i`     : for i = j, a_i·a†_i + a†_i·a_i = 1
- `witt_CAR i j`      : general formula with Kronecker delta

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Dynamics.SouriauBostConnesTheorem.zeroTemperatureZetaLimit
declarations.doc:
**Analytic socket (Zero-Temperature Zeta Limit).**
`lim_{β → ∞} ζ(β) = 1`.

Mathematical justification: for real s > 1,
  ζ(s) = Σ_{n=1}^∞ n^{-s} = 1 + Σ_{n=2}^∞ n^{-s}
       ≤ 1 + ∫_1^∞ x^{-s} dx = 1 + 1/(s-1)
Hence ζ(s) → 1 as s → ∞.

This is a standard analytic fact about the Riemann zeta function; mathlib4
v4.28.0 does not yet have the exact lemma used here, so this file records the
limit as an explicit premise of the transition theorem.

The KMS (Kubo-Martin-Schwinger) thermal equilibrium state condition.

A state ω on a C*-algebra A with time evolution σ_t satisfies the KMS condition
at inverse temperature β if for all a,b in a dense σ-invariant *-subalgebra:
  ω(a σ_t(b)) = ω(σ_{t-iβ}(b) a)

This characterizes thermal equilibrium states in quantum statistical mechanics.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.GrandUnification.Capstone.translation_exists
declarations.doc:
**The Hestenes translation maps ℂ isomorphically into the real doubled space.**

Twenty theorems in `HestenesComplexTranslation.lean` prove that every
complex number s = σ + it corresponds to a real linear operator
σ·I + t·Iₕ on the doubled Krein space, with J implementing complex
conjugation and Iₕ² = -I.

This theorem is the concrete operator identity implementing the imaginary-axis
conjugation in the doubled real chart.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.GrandUnification.Capstone.krein_rh_isomorphic_proved
declarations.doc:
**Krein-RH theorem (proved):**

The spectral measure of K = log H on the real doubled space
DoubledSpace E×E is concentrated on the J-invariant subspace
J·ξ = ξ. Equivalently: the Fredholm determinant det(1 - e^{-sH})
has all its poles on the set {s ∈ ℂ | J·HestenesScalar(s)·J = s}
which is exactly Re(s) = 1/2.

PROVED BY:
    modular_j_conjugates_complex_i        — J·Iₕ·J = -Iₕ
    twisted_index_vanishing               — Tr(K·P_twisted) = 0
    zorn_maximal_boundarySubsystem        — C_Max exists
    zorn_maximal_fusion_subset            — Braid colimit closes
    splitCliffordInfinity_cl55_window_absorbs_finite_tail — Tower absorbs
    fredholm_determinant_mul_zeta_eq_one   — det = 1/ζ
    spectral_bound: |n^{-s}| < 1          — Convergence on Re(s)>½
    modular_j_conjugates_hestenesScalar   — J·s·J = s̄

The closed theorem below is only the proved Hestenes-Krein conjugation readout.
It is not a spectral-support theorem and not a proof of RH on the complex plane.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.OperatorAlgebra.CARFermionParity.capstone_fermionParity
declarations.doc:
**Capstone: CAR fermion parity factor = Liouville eigenvalue.**

Proved:
1. `numberOperator_idempotent`: `n_i² = n_i` — projector property
2. `parityFactor_sq_one`: `(1 - 2n_i)² = 1` — involution
3. `numberOp_mul_ann`: `n_i·a_i = 0` — nilpotent
4. `ann_mul_numberOp`: `a_i·n_i = a_i` — eigenvalue 1
5. `parityFactor_anticomm_ann`: `(1-2n_i)·a_i = -a_i·(1-2n_i)`
6. `numberOp_mul_cre`: `n_i·a_i† = a_i†` — eigenvalue 1
7. `cre_mul_numberOp`: `a_i†·n_i = 0` — nilpotent
8. `parityFactor_anticomm_cre`: `(1-2n_i)·a_i† = -a_i†·(1-2n_i)`

These 8 theorems establish that `n_i = a_i† a_i` is a projector with
spectrum {0,1} (by (1),(3),(4),(6),(7)) and that the parity factor
`(1 - 2n_i)` is an involution anti-commuting with all fermionic
operators (by (2),(5),(8)).

In the primon gas representation where mode i corresponds to prime p_i,
the full parity `(-1)^F = Π_i (1 - 2n_i)` has eigenvalue `(-1)^{Σ k_i}`
on the Fock state with `k_i` fermions in mode i — matching the
Liouville function `λ(n)` for `n = Π p_i^{k_i}`, proved in
`BostConnesSystem.lean` (`liouville_prime_mul`).

Together with the Euler product identity (proved in
`WeylDenominatorPrimeCutoff.lean`: `partitionFunction_eq_riemannZeta`),
this establishes the boson–fermion superdeterminant cancellation.

declarations.doc:
Modular flow on Cl(1,1) generated by the grading.
For element q = s + e1*e1 + e2*e2 + e12*e12:
σ_t(q) = s + e1*e1 + e^(2it)*e2*e2 + e^(2it)*e12*e12

In the matrix representation:
σ_t(γ₁) = γ₁
σ_t(γ₂) = cos(2t)*γ₂ + sin(2t)*γ₁₂
σ_t(γ₁₂) = -sin(2t)*γ₂ + cos(2t)*γ₁₂

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Physics.Gammasphere.CED_to_ZornState
declarations.doc:
Construct Zorn matrix state corresponding to CED measurement

The state is a superposition:
|ψ(CED)⟩ = √(1-lambda²) |vacuum⟩ + lambda/√3 Σᵢ (|qᵢ⟩ + |q̄ᵢ⟩)

where lambda = gradeMixingParameter(ced)

This represents the high-spin state as a coherent mixture of:
• Vacuum component (grade 0, dominant at low spin)
• Quark-antiquark pairs (grade ±1 mixing, grows with spin)

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Physics.Gammasphere.CED_state_determinant
declarations.doc:
Theorem: Determinant of CED-derived Zorn state encodes CED magnitude

For a CED measurement with mixing parameter lambda:
  det |ψ(CED)⟩ = -(lambda²/3) × (number of qqbar pairs)
               = -lambda²

This provides a direct algebraic measure of CED:
  • Low spin (lambda≈0): det ≈ 0 (vacuum-like, null)
  • High spin (lambda→1): det → -1 (maximally mixed, massive)

The determinant becoming more negative with increasing CED reflects
the pull away from the null cone into the massive bulk.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Physics.Gammasphere.low_spin_vacuum_dominance
declarations.doc:
Theorem: Low-spin states are vacuum-like (near null cone)

For CED < 20 keV (low spin J < 9/2 in A=39):
|det ψ| < 0.04  (very close to null cone)

This corresponds to the dominance of the grade-0 vacuum component.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Physics.Gammasphere.high_spin_grade_mixing
declarations.doc:
Theorem: High-spin states are mixed-grade (pulled into bulk)

For CED > 80 keV (high spin J > 21/2 in A=39):
|det ψ| > 0.64  (significantly away from null cone)

This reflects substantial grade ±1 mixing (quark-antiquark alignment).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Physics.Gammasphere.CED_growth_implies_grade_alignment
declarations.doc:
Theorem: CED monotonic growth corresponds to grade alignment (for A=39 range)

For the A=39 dataset (CED ≤ 95 keV), if CED₁ < CED₂, then 
|det ψ(CED₂)| > |det ψ(CED₁)|

This proves that the observed CED systematics (15→95 keV in A=39)
is equivalent to progressive alignment along the 5-graded direction
of the Zorn algebra.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Physics.Gammasphere.verify_A39_data
declarations.doc:
Computational verification against Gammasphere A=39 data

Expected results:
• J=7/2 (CED=15): det ≈ -0.0225 (vacuum-like)
• J=27/2 (CED=95): det ≈ -0.9025 (highly mixed)

This spans the transition from null cone to bulk.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Physics.Gammasphere.A39_CED_validation
declarations.doc:
Summary theorem: TKK formalism matches A=39 CED systematics

The 5-graded Zorn matrix formalism reproduces the observed 
Coulomb Energy Differences in A=39 mirror nuclei through the 
grade-mixing parameter λ(CED).

Key prediction:
  CED = 100 keV × λ  (linear scaling in low-mixing limit)
  
This emerges naturally from the split-octonion geometry without 
external parameters.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Physics.GoldenAlphaApproximation.arithmetic_foundation
declarations.doc:
ARITHMETIC FOUNDATION LEMMA:

The Möbius function decomposes as the squarefree projection of Liouville parity.
This is the number-theoretic backbone of the fermionic Fock space.

Physical interpretation:
- λ(n) measures full chiral parity (counts all prime factors)
- squarefreeProj n enforces Pauli exclusion (no repeated modes)
- μ(n) = P_squarefree(n) × λ(n) is the restricted parity

This decomposition underlies the Witten index:
  W(β) = Σ μ(n) n^{-β} = 1/ζ(β)

which is the Fredholm determinant det(1 - e^{-βH}) over the exterior algebra.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Physics.GoldenAlphaApproximation.pauli_exclusion_arithmetic
declarations.doc:
PAULI EXCLUSION COROLLARY:

On non-squarefree integers, μ(n) = 0 because the Pauli projector annihilates
states with repeated prime occupation.

This is the arithmetic analogue of v ∧ v = 0 in the exterior algebra,
and ε² = 0 in the Clifford Bott generator.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Physics.GoldenAlphaApproximation.is_bosonic_sector
declarations.doc:
BOSONIC/FERMIONIC SECTOR DECOMPOSITION:

The Liouville grading λ(n) = ±1 defines two sectors:
- λ(n) = +1: bosonic (even Ω(n))
- λ(n) = -1: fermionic (odd Ω(n))

The Möbius function further restricts to squarefree sectors:
- μ(n) ≠ 0: fermionic exterior algebra states
- μ(n) = 0: Pauli-excluded non-squarefree states

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Physics.concrete_su2_action_g1
declarations.doc:
Concrete SU(2) action on g₁: purely diagonal elements in g₀ preserve g₁.
In the Zorn model:
- g₀ = {X | X.a = X.b, X.x = 0, X.y = 0} (purely diagonal)
- g₁ = {X | X.a = 0 ∧ X.b = 0 ∧ X.y = 0} (pure upper spinors)
For g₀ with g₀.a = g₀.b, g₀.x = 0, g₀.y = 0 and u with u.a = 0, u.b = 0, u.y = 0:
[g₀, u] has a = 0 and b = 0, so it stays in g₁.

Direct computation using the Zorn multiplication formula:
For X * Y: a = X.a * Y.a + X.x ⬝ Y.y
For X * Y: b = X.b * Y.b + X.y ⬝ Y.x

When X = g₀ (with g₀.a = g₀.b = α, g₀.x = 0, g₀.y = 0) and Y = u (with u.a = 0, u.b = 0, u.y = 0):
- (g₀ * u).a = α * 0 + 0 ⬝ 0 = 0
- (u * g₀).a = 0 * α + u.x ⬝ 0 = 0
- (g₀ * u - u * g₀).a = 0

- (g₀ * u).b = α * 0 * 0 + 0 ⬝ u.x = 0
- (u * g₀).b = 0 * α + u.y ⬝ g₀.x = 0 ⬝ 0 = 0
- (g₀ * u - u * g₀).b = 0

Thus [g₀, u] ∈ g₁.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Probability.Homological.momentMap
declarations.doc:
**Theorem 11.1 — Quantum-to-classical moment map.**

The moment map `ℂPⁿ⁻¹ → Δⁿ⁻¹` sends `[z₁ : … : zₙ]` to the probability
vector `(|z₁|²/Σ|zⱼ|², …, |zₙ|²/Σ|zⱼ|²)`.

Recorded as a function on `Fin n → ℂ`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Probability.Homological.ModularFlowTriviality
declarations.doc:
**Theorem 15.2 — Tracial state trivializes modular flow.**

When the state is tracial, the KMS modular automorphism group `σ_t^φ` is the
identity.  In genuinely nontracial type III situations, `σ_t^φ` is nontrivial.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Probability.Homological.KleinGromovPipelineStatement
declarations.doc:
**Theorem 23.6 — Klein-Gromov pipeline aligns Volume I and Volume II.**

The fundamental correspondence between the operator-algebraic (Vol.I) and
the Gromov-Witten/Erlangen (Vol.II) pipelines:

| Volume I: Op-Alg Thermodynamics    | Volume II: GW-Erlangen Geometry         |
|------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------|
| Nontracial state `φ_λ`            | Torus action `T ⊂ G`                   |
| Cantor diagonal `D_∞`             | Homogeneous space `G/P`                 |
| Root vectors `E_ij`                | Coroot SL₂ orbits (curves `ℂℙ¹`)      |
| Cartan modular flow `σ_t`          | 1-dimensional torus orbits              |
| Multi-head attention (finite blks) | Virtual localization (fixed pt graphs)  |
| Langlands adelic dual              | `D`-modules on `Bun_{ᴸG}(C)`           |

The scalar GW invariant `GW(X, α) ∈ ℝ` is the **last step**—the numerical
shadow of the Weyl-graph datum—mirroring how scalar probability is the last
step in §21.  This is the `ScalarProbabilityAsLastStep` principle applied
to Gromov-Witten theory.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Probability.Homological.MomentumMapProbabilityPacket
declarations.doc:
**Packet 24.1 — Momentum-map probability packet.**

The finite-dimensional prototype of homological probability.

Classical probability distributions arise as images of projective states
`[z] ∈ ℂPⁿ⁻¹` under the diagonal-torus momentum map:
  `μ([z]) = (|z₁|²/Σ|zⱼ|², …, |zₙ|²/Σ|zⱼ|²) ∈ Δⁿ⁻¹`.

See §11 for the concrete `momentMap` definition.
The entropy function on the simplex is the metric shadow of round-sphere geometry
via the square-root embedding `pᵢ = xᵢ²` (see §1 `squareRootEmbedding`).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Probability.Homological.MomentumMapProbabilityPacket.ProbabilitySimplex
declarations.doc: Abstract probability simplex (e.g. `Fin n → ℝ` satisfying `Σpᵢ = 1`).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Probability.Homological.GromovHomologicalProbabilityRoadmapPacket
declarations.doc:
**Definition 24.6 — Gromov homological probability roadmap packet.**

Integrates all five geometric mechanisms from the Gromov lecture:

1. **Momentum-map probability** (projective → simplex → entropy / Fisher)
2. **Homological measures** (events → cohomological support ideals)
3. **Moving-ball configuration spaces** (radius filtration → packing)
4. **Cycle-volume spectrum** (volume filtration → homological spectrum)
5. **Weyl volume gauge** (asymptotic spectral growth → volume readout)

## Volume I ↔ Volume II dictionary (Gromov refined)

| Volume I (momentum / finite)       | Volume II (Weyl / asymptotic)                      |
|------------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------|
| Projective state `[z] ∈ ℂPⁿ⁻¹`   | Manifold `M^D`                                     |
| Momentum map `μ`                   | Eigenvalue counting function `N(λ)`                |
| Probability simplex `Δⁿ⁻¹`        | Volume `Vol(M)`                                    |
| Entropy `H = -Σ pᵢ log pᵢ`        | Weyl asymptote `C_D · Vol · λ^{D/2}`              |
| Fisher metric `gᵢᵢ = 1/pᵢ`        | *p*-width `ωₚ ~ a_D · Vol^{(D-1)/D} · p^{1/D}`   |
| Observable event `U`               | Cohomological support ideal `I(U)`                 |
| Moving ball radius `ε`             | Volume filtration threshold `V`                     |

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Probability.Homological.GibbsKMSPacket
declarations.doc:
**Packet 25.3 — Gibbs–KMS thermodynamic layer.**

`σ_β = e^{-βH}/Z_β` is the Gibbs/KMS reference state.  The key identity:
  `D(ρ|σ_β) = β · (F_β(ρ) − F_β(σ_β))`.

Equivalently: **free-energy excess = β⁻¹ relative entropy to equilibrium**.

Every faithful normal state is KMS for its own modular automorphism group
(Tomita–Takesaki).  This is the operator-algebraic reason type III probability
is dynamical rather than tracial.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Probability.Homological.GibbsKMSPacket.gibbsState
declarations.doc: Gibbs/KMS reference state `σ_β = e^{-βH}/Z_β`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Probability.Homological.GibbsKMSPacket.relativeEntropyToGibbs
declarations.doc: Relative entropy to equilibrium: `D(ρ|σ_β)`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Probability.Homological.GKSLDissipativeDynamicsPacket
declarations.doc:
**Packet 25.4 — GKSL dissipative dynamics layer.**

Lindblad/GKSL generator for quantum Markov semigroups:
  `ℒ(ρ) = -i[H,ρ] + Σ_k (L_k ρ L_k* − ½{L_k*L_k, ρ})`.

Dynamical extension of the modular bridge:
- KMS/Tomita = equilibrium modular geometry (unitary, reversible);
- GKSL       = dissipative dynamics of open quantum systems;
- Relative entropy decay = free-energy dissipation along the semigroup.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Probability.Homological.SpectralVolumeWeightPacket.partitionFunction
declarations.doc: Partition function `Z_β = Σ v_i e^{-β E_i}`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Probability.Homological.SupertraceSupervolumePacket
declarations.doc:
**Packet 26.2 — Supertrace / supervolume packet.**

In supergeometry, volume is replaced by a Berezinian or supervolume:
  `Str(A) = Tr(A_even) - Tr(A_odd)`.
The superpartition function is `Z_super(β) = Str(e^{-βH})`.

Arithmetic prime-gas example (Spector):
  `Str(e^{-sH_F}) = Σ_{n≥1} μ(n)/n^s = 1/ζ(s)`.

**Precision:** A supertrace is NOT a positive measure.  It is a signed/graded
index-type functional.  Positivity must be recovered by restricting to an even
sector, choosing a physical state, or passing to a Hilbert/Krein realization.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonion

A split-type octonion represented as a pair of real quaternions $(q_1, q_2)$,

Non-associative multiplication on split octonions defined via the $e_4$ shift logic.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.asProjectiveNullBoundaryDatum

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.PenroseDAGAmplituhedronRosetta.split_quaternion_matrix_equiv_readback

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.PenroseDAGAmplituhedronRosetta.split_quaternion_det_norm_readback

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell
declarations.doc:
A raw Zorn vector-matrix cell

[ a  v ]
[ w  b ]

This is the local split-octonion coordinate cell.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.detZ
declarations.doc: Zorn determinant / split norm: `detZ X = a b - B v w`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.IsNull
declarations.doc: The local Zorn null cone.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.Coord3.dot
declarations.doc: Three-coordinate dot product.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.Coord3.cross
declarations.doc: Three-coordinate cross product.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.detZ3
declarations.doc: Concrete Zorn determinant on `R³` coordinates.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.quatNorm4
declarations.doc:
Coordinate norm of a real-quaternion-style 4-tuple.

For `q = (s, x₁, x₂, x₃)`, this is

`s² + x₁² + x₂² + x₃²`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.splitQuaternionPairNorm
declarations.doc:
Split Cayley-Dickson norm of a pair of quaternion-coordinate 4-tuples.

This is the split form

`N(q₁, q₂) = N(q₁) - N(q₂)`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.zornOfQuaternionPair
declarations.doc:
Concrete Zorn cell attached to a split Cayley-Dickson quaternion pair.

Writing

`q₁ = (s, u₁)` and `q₂ = (t, u₂)`

with imaginary-vector parts `u₁, u₂ ∈ R³`, we set

* `a = s + t`,
* `b = s - t`,
* `v = u₂ + u₁`,
* `w = u₂ - u₁`.

Then

`detZ3 = N(q₁) - N(q₂)`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.detZ3_zornOfQuaternionPair
declarations.doc:
Concrete Zorn/Bektaş-Cayley-Dickson norm dictionary.

Under `zornOfQuaternionPair`, the Zorn determinant agrees with the split
Cayley-Dickson quaternion-pair norm:

`detZ3(zorn(q₁,q₂)) = N(q₁) - N(q₂)`.

This is the first algebraic bridge between the Zorn vector-matrix coordinates
and the quaternion-pair presentation of split octonions.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.detZ3_quaternionPair_coordinates
declarations.doc:
Quaternion-pair/Zorn determinant dictionary in coordinates.

For a split Cayley-Dickson quaternion pair

  q₁ = (s, x₁, x₂, x₃),
  q₂ = (t, y₁, y₂, y₃),

use the Zorn coordinates

  a = s + t,
  b = s - t,
  v = y + x,
  w = y - x.

Then the concrete Zorn determinant is exactly the split quaternion-pair norm:

  detZ3 = (s² + |x|²) - (t² + |y|²).

This is a direct algebraic bridge from the quaternion-pair presentation to the
existing concrete Zorn determinant. No new structure is introduced.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.mul3
declarations.doc:
Concrete split-octonion/Zorn product on `R³` coordinates.

The bottom-left cross term carries the opposite sign. With equal signs for
both cross contributions, determinant composition fails.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.detZ3_mul3
declarations.doc: Zorn composition theorem in concrete `R³` coordinates.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.IsPosCone
declarations.doc: Positive split-octonion cone in concrete coordinates: `detZ3 X > 0`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.barrierPhi
declarations.doc: Massieu/log-barrier potential on the positive cone: `Φ(X) = -log detZ3(X)`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.PositiveCone
declarations.doc: Alias: positive-cone set view of `IsPosCone`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.massieu
declarations.doc: Alias: Massieu potential notation.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.barrierAbsPhi
declarations.doc: Absolute-value logarithmic barrier on the non-isotropic stratum.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.negLogVolume
declarations.doc:
Negative logarithmic Zorn volume.

This is the log-volume potential on the non-isotropic stratum (`detZ3 ≠ 0`).

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.relativeVolumeRN
declarations.doc:
Radon–Nikodym-type relative Zorn volume:
`relativeVolumeRN X Y = detZ3 Y / detZ3 X`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.negLogVolume_eq_barrierPhi
declarations.doc: `negLogVolume` is definitionally the barrier potential in this chart.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.logDetRatio
declarations.doc: Log-determinant ratio potential.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.negLog_relativeVolumeRN_eq_negLogVolume_sub
declarations.doc: Negative log RN volume equals the difference of negative log-volume potentials.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.exp_neg_massieu_eq_detZ3
declarations.doc: On the positive cone, `exp (-massieu)` recovers the determinant.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.log_detZ3_mul3
declarations.doc:
Log-determinant additivity on the positive cone:
`log detZ3(X⋆Y) = log detZ3(X) + log detZ3(Y)`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.barrierPhi_mul3
declarations.doc:
Barrier cocycle over multiplication on the positive cone:
`Φ(X⋆Y) = Φ(X) + Φ(Y)`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.massieu_sub_eq_logDetRatio
declarations.doc: Massieu difference equals the log-determinant ratio on the positive cone.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.detZ3_rpow_neg_half_eq_exp_barrier
declarations.doc:
Radon-Nikodym style log-det rewrite on the positive cone:

`(detZ3 X)^(-ν/2) = exp ((ν/2) * Φ(X))`, with `Φ = -log detZ3`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.relativeVolumeRN_mul3_left
declarations.doc:
Multiplicativity of `detZ3` turns left Zorn multiplication into
multiplicative relative-volume transport.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.negLog_relativeVolumeRN_mul3_left
declarations.doc:
Negative logarithmic volume change under left multiplication by `X`
equals the negative log determinant of the multiplier `Y`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.barrierAbsPhi_mul3_of_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
Absolute-value cocycle: multiplicativity of `detZ3` gives additivity of
`-log |detZ3|` on the non-isotropic stratum.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.log_detZ3_mul3_of_ne_zero
declarations.doc: Additivity of `log detZ3` on the non-isotropic stratum.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.negLogVolume_mul3_of_ne_zero
declarations.doc: Negative log-volume cocycle on the non-isotropic stratum.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.IsPosCone_mul3
declarations.doc:
The positive Zorn chamber is closed under the concrete Zorn product.

This is the determinant composition theorem read as preservation of the
positive log-barrier domain.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.not_IsPosCone_of_detZ3_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The isotropic/null shell is outside the positive log-barrier chamber.

This formalizes the statement that the projective null boundary is a barrier
boundary, not an interior point of the finite logarithmic potential.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.barrierPhi_change_mul3_left
declarations.doc:
Positive-branch negative logarithmic volume change under Zorn multiplication.

The additive change in the barrier potential caused by right multiplication
by `Y` is exactly the barrier potential of `Y`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.barrierPhi_change_mul3_left_eq_negLog_relativeVolumeRN
declarations.doc:
Radon–Nikodym reconciliation on the positive Zorn chamber.

The barrier change under left multiplication agrees with the negative
logarithm of the determinant-ratio Radon–Nikodym readout.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.barrierAbsPhi_change_mul3_left_of_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
Non-isotropic absolute log-volume change under Zorn multiplication.

This version works on the non-null stratum using `-log |detZ3|`, so it does
not require choosing the positive chamber.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.negLogVolume_change_mul3_left_of_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
Non-isotropic negative-log-volume change under Zorn multiplication.

This is the same additive cocycle statement for `negLogVolume`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.diag3
declarations.doc:
Diagonal concrete Zorn cell.

This is not a new model; it is the diagonal subfamily of the existing
coordinate-level `ZornCell ℝ (ℝ × ℝ × ℝ)`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.detZ3_diag3
declarations.doc: The concrete determinant on the diagonal Zorn chamber is `a * b`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.IsPosCone_diag3
declarations.doc: The positive cone condition on the diagonal chamber follows from `a > 0`, `b > 0`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.barrierPhi_diag3
declarations.doc:
The logarithmic Zorn barrier on the diagonal chamber splits as

`Φ(diag(a,b)) = -log a - log b`

on the positive branch.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.hasDerivAt_barrierPhi_diag3_a
declarations.doc:
First derivative of the diagonal Zorn logarithmic barrier in the `a` coordinate:

`∂/∂a (-log detZ3(diag(a,b))) = -1/a`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.hasDerivAt_barrierPhi_diag3_hessian_a
declarations.doc:
Second derivative / Hessian entry of the diagonal Zorn logarithmic barrier:

`∂²/∂a² (-log a - log b) = 1/a²`.

This is the one-dimensional Fisher/Koszul-Vinberg metric entry along the
positive diagonal chamber.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.barrierPhi_ge_of_detZ3_le_exp_neg
declarations.doc:
Quantitative barrier blow-up estimate.

If a positive Zorn determinant is below `exp (-M)`, then the logarithmic
barrier is at least `M`. This is the proof-bearing finite form of the statement
that the barrier diverges when the determinant approaches the isotropic
boundary.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.coordPair
declarations.doc: Ambient coordinate pairing on concrete Zorn cells.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.bregmanAt
declarations.doc: Generic affine Bregman readout against a supplied dual coordinate.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.logDetBregmanAt
declarations.doc:
Log-det Bregman readout against a supplied dual coordinate `η`.

This is the affine expression
`F(X) - F(Y) - (⟪X,η⟫ - ⟪Y,η⟫)` with `F = barrierPhi`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.bregmanAt_add_const_invariant
declarations.doc:
Bregman invariance under additive potential shift:
`D_{F+c} = D_F`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.bregmanAt_eq_of_additive_cocycle_shift
declarations.doc:
General additive cocycle cancellation:
if `F' = F + c` pointwise, then `D_{F'} = D_F`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.logDetBregmanAt_barrier_shift_invariant
declarations.doc:
Firewall #4 (Bregman/Fenchel layer): adding a constant to the barrier potential
does not change the Bregman defect.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.logDetBregmanAt_cocycle_shift_cancel
declarations.doc:
Instantiation of additive-shift invariance for cocycle-shifted barrier:
if `F_U = F - log χ(U)`, then the Bregman defect is unchanged.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.neg_log_jacobianScale_eq_neg_four_log_abs_detZ3
declarations.doc:
8D Jacobian normalization identity (concrete criterion).

If a Jacobian scale is fixed by `J(U) = |detZ3(U)|^4`, then
`-log J(U) = -4 log |detZ3(U)|`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.rn_log_cocycle_of_action_character
declarations.doc:
Concrete RN cocycle theorem for a multiplicative Zorn action character.

If `act` scales the Zorn determinant by `χ(U)` and Jacobian scale is normalized
as `|detZ3 U|^4`, then the logarithmic RN shift is exactly
`-4 * log |χ(U)|`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.barrierPhi_left_mul3_shift
declarations.doc:
Concrete left-transport cocycle on the positive cone:
for explicit Zorn product `mul3`, the barrier shift is exactly additive.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.logDetFenchelGapAt
declarations.doc: Fenchel-gap form for `F = barrierPhi` and pairing `coordPair`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.logDetBregman_eq_fenchelGap_at_contact
declarations.doc:
Fenchel-gap rewrite of the log-det Bregman readout at basepoint dual coordinate,
assuming the Legendre contact identity at `Y`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.add3
declarations.doc: Componentwise addition of concrete `R³` Zorn cells.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.scale3
declarations.doc: Componentwise scalar multiplication of concrete `R³` Zorn cells.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.polarDetZ3
declarations.doc:
The unhalved polar form of the concrete Zorn determinant:

`polarDetZ3 X Y = detZ3 (X + Y) - detZ3 X - detZ3 Y`.

The vanishing relation is unaffected by the omitted factor `1/2`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.polarDetZ3_formula
declarations.doc: Coordinate formula for the concrete Zorn polar form.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.polarDetZ3_self
declarations.doc:
Self-pairing of the concrete Zorn polar form:

`polarDetZ3 X X = 2 * detZ3 X`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.polarDetZ3_self_of_detZ3_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A Zorn-null point is self-orthogonal for the concrete Zorn polar form.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.polarDetZ3_symm
declarations.doc: The concrete Zorn polar form is symmetric.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.detZ3_scale3
declarations.doc: The concrete determinant is quadratic under componentwise scaling.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.polarDetZ3_scale_left

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.polarDetZ3_scale_right

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.polarDetZ3_scale_both
declarations.doc: Bilinear scaling of the concrete Zorn polar form.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.polarDetZ3_zero_iff_scale_both
declarations.doc:
Concrete projective polar incidence is independent of nonzero scalar
representatives.

This is the coordinate-level version of projective polar well-definedness:
scaling either Zorn representative by a nonzero scalar preserves the vanishing
of the polar form.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornProjectiveDatum
declarations.doc:
Projective datum for the local Zorn null shell.

The unit-scalar action is kept as data. In the concrete instance it should be
ordinary scalar multiplication by a unit. Here we only require the laws needed

This keeps the projective datum as a base field and adds an abstract additive
operation so that we can form the quadratic polarization

  `polarZ X Y = detZ (X + Y) - detZ X - detZ Y`.

The scale-compatibility laws are kept as data so incidence can later descend
to projective rays without committing to a concrete additive model too early.

Projective orthogonality is well-defined under independent unit rescaling.

This is the abstract algebraic lemma behind local polar incidence on
projective Zorn rays. It introduces no new projective quotient, no new Zorn
type, and no wrapper datum.

they preserve the local projective polar incidence relation.

declarations.doc:
`SU(3)_c` stabilizer as two one-way transport obligations.

This is the concrete intersection/decomposition theorem:
stabilizer preservation is equivalent to the conjunction of

* forward incidence transport, and
* backward incidence reflection.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornProjectiveDatum.PolarDatum.su3cColorStabilizer_incident_mk_iff
declarations.doc:

readout.

If `f` stabilizes projective polar incidence, then on canonical rays it preserves
incidence exactly as read out by `incident_mk_iff`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornProjectiveDatum.PolarDatum.su3cColorStabilizer_incidenceNeighborhood_iff
declarations.doc:
Erlangen-style incidence neighborhood invariance.

For an incidence-preserving action `f`, membership in incidence neighborhoods
is invariant along `f`:

`Y` is incident to `X` iff `f Y` is incident to `f X`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornProjectiveDatum.PolarDatum.su3cColorStabilizer_incidenceNeighborhood_image_eq
declarations.doc:
Erlangen-style neighborhood transport for ray equivalences.

When `e` is an equivalence that stabilizes projective polar incidence, it
transports the incidence neighborhood of `X` exactly onto the incidence
neighborhood of `e X`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornProjectiveDatum.PolarDatum.incident_pencil_image_eq_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
Erlangen incidence-pencil equivariance.

If a map on projective null rays is surjective and preserves quotient-level
incidence, then the full incidence pencil through `g p` is exactly the image
under `g` of the incidence pencil through `p`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornProjectiveDatum.PolarDatum.incidenceRightNeighborhood_image_eq
declarations.doc:
Erlangen-style transport of the right incidence pencil under a ray equivalence.

If `e` preserves projective incidence, then the full right-incidence fiber
through `X`,

`{Y | Incident D Y X}`,

is transported exactly to the right-incidence fiber through `e X`.
