declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ProjectivePolarFiberTransport.incidenceFiber_image_eq
declarations.doc:
A group action preserving the polar form up to a scalar factor transports
incidence fibers exactly.

This is the concrete Erlangen/twistor statement:

  `Set.image (act g) (incidenceFiber polar X)
     = incidenceFiber polar (act g X)`.

It says the incidence-defined “celestial sphere” attached to `X` is not tied to
coordinates; it is carried functorially by the symmetry action.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ProjectivePolarFiberTransport.mem_incidenceFiber_iff_exists_preimage
declarations.doc:
Membership form of `incidenceFiber_image_eq`.

This is often the easier theorem for downstream rewriting:
`Y` is incident with `gX` iff it is the image of something incident with `X`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ProjectivePolarInvariant.projective_incidence_well_defined
declarations.doc:
Projective polar incidence is well-defined under independent nonzero scalar
rescaling of representatives.

If

  B(λ • X, Y) = λ * B(X,Y)

and

  B(X, μ • Y) = μ * B(X,Y),

then for nonzero `λ` and `μ`,

  B(X,Y)=0 ↔ B(λ • X, μ • Y)=0.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ProjectivePolarInvariant.projective_incidence_scaled_of_zero
declarations.doc:
Forward-only form.

Zero polar incidence is preserved by arbitrary scalar rescaling. This direction
does not require nonzero scalars and does not require `NoZeroDivisors`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ProjectivePolarInvariant.incidence_invariant_of_polar_scaled
declarations.doc:
Erlangen-style incidence invariance under a symmetry action.

If a symmetry action preserves the polar form up to a nonzero scalar factor,

B(gX,gY) = χ(g) * B(X,Y),

then the zero-incidence relation is invariant:

B(X,Y)=0 ↔ B(gX,gY)=0.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ProjectivePolarInvariant.projective_erlangen_incidence_invariant
declarations.doc:
Combined projective-plus-Erlangen incidence invariance.

If representatives are rescaled by nonzero scalars and then acted on by a
symmetry preserving the polar form up to a nonzero factor, incidence is
unchanged:

  B(X,Y)=0
    ↔
  B(g(λX), g(μY))=0.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.normalized_logdet_stable_of_square
declarations.doc:
Finite-stage normalized log-determinant stabilization.

This is the algebraic core behind the determinant stabilization in the
tensor-doubling tower. If the next-stage determinant is the square of the
current-stage determinant, then the volume-normalized log determinant is
unchanged:

`log(det_{N+1}) / 2^(N+1) = log(det_N) / 2^N`.

This is the finite theorem behind the trace-log / Fuglede-Kadison intuition.
It does not assert the existence of an infinite von Neumann algebra limit.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.normalized_logdet_stage_stable
declarations.doc:
Stage-function version of normalized log-determinant stabilization.

Use this when a finite tower has determinant values `detStage N` and the
bonding step satisfies `detStage (N+1) = detStage N ^ 2`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.zornRelativeVolumeRN
declarations.doc:

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.detZ_scalarScale_pos
declarations.doc:
The determinant remains positive under componentwise unit scaling.

This is the domain-preservation theorem for the positive log-volume chart.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.zornLogBarrier_scalarScale
declarations.doc:
Log-barrier shift under Zorn unit scaling.

Since

detZ(u • X) = u² detZ(X),

we get

-log detZ(u • X) = -log detZ(X) - log(u²)

on the positive determinant stratum.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.zornRelativeVolumeRN_self
declarations.doc:
The relative Zorn volume of a point with itself is `1`
on the non-isotropic stratum.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornCell.negLog_zornRelativeVolumeRN_eq_zornLogBarrier_sub
declarations.doc:
The negative logarithm of the Zorn RN relative-volume factor is the
difference of log-barrier potentials:

  -log(detZ(Y)/detZ(X)) = φ(Y) - φ(X),

where `φ(X) = -log detZ(X)`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornMatrix
declarations.doc:
A Zorn vector matrix following Voelkel's Convention 3.1.12.
$x^{11}$ and $x^{12}$ are the diagonal scalar components.
$x^{21}$ and $x^{22}$ are the off-diagonal vector components.
Notice the structural minus sign on $x^{22}$ is absorbed into the definition of the operations.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornMatrix.norm

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornMatrix.mul
declarations.doc:
The Zorn matrix non-associative product (Voelkel page 34).
This explicitly omits the cross product, using only the Euclidean scalar product.
The non-associativity arises strictly from the `A (B \cdot C) \neq B (A \cdot C)` mismatch!

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornMatrix.diag_assoc_mid
declarations.doc: Voelkel Lemma 3.1.13 (2): `(x * χ) * y = x * (χ * y)` when `χ` is diagonal.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Projective.SplitOctonions.ZornMatrix.diag_assoc_left
declarations.doc: Voelkel Lemma 3.1.13 (3): `(χ * x) * y = χ * (x * y)` when `χ` is diagonal.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Quantum.PauliSoldering.capstone_all_lemmas_proved
declarations.doc:
The **supercharge → momentum dictionary** is now complete with genuine lemmas:

1. `σPlus_sq`, `σMinus_sq` — nilpotent chiral generators
2. `commutator_σPlus_σMinus` — [σ+, σ-] = σ³ (sl(2,ℂ) algebra)
3. `solder_explicit` — P_spinor = [[E+pz, px-ipy], [px+ipy, E-pz]]
4. `casimir_as_determinant` — det(P_spinor) = P_μ P^μ
5. `inverse_pauli_trace` — P_μ = ½ Tr(σ_μ P_spinor)
6. `null_momentum_factorization` — P = λ λ† for massless
7. `null_momentum_det_zero` — det = 0 for massless twistors
8. `σPlus_adjoint`, `σ3_adjoint` — Hermiticity of chiral basis
9. `solder_hermitian` — P_spinor is Hermitian for real momentum
10. `trace_solder_eq_two_E` — Tr(P_spinor) = 2E
11. `det_solder_eq_zero_iff_lightlike` — det = 0 ↔ lightlike

All 11 theorems are `fin_cases` kernel-checked, 0 sorries.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Quantum.PoincareSupercharge.casimir_sq
declarations.doc:
The Casimir P^μ P_μ = H² - p² = H² in the rest frame.
From `H_pow_eq n ε 2` we get H² = Σ ε_i² P_i.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Quantum.PoincareSupercharge.primon_casimir_eigenvalues
declarations.doc:
The finite primon Hamiltonian `H = Σ log(p_i) P_i` has Casimir eigenvalues
`(log p_i)²` on the corresponding Cuntz range projectors.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Quantum.PoincareSupercharge.pauli_supercharge_trace_recovers_four_momentum

The Pauli trace formula recovers the four-momentum components from the
super-Poincare anticommutator matrix `2 σ^μ P_μ`.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Quantum.PoincareSupercharge.pauli_supercharge_trace_recovers_lowered_four_momentum
declarations.doc:
The lowered Pauli trace formula recovers the metric-lowered four-momentum
components from the same super-Poincare anticommutator matrix.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Quantum.PoincareSupercharge.pauli_supercharge_anticommutator_det_eq_four_casimir

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Quantum.PoincareSupercharge.pauli_supercharge_anticommutator_trace_eq_four_energy

In the triality kernel, multiplication by a vector is represented by the

operator on the doubled space.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.Quantum.SplitTrialityKernel.k_acts_as_imaginary
declarations.doc:
The Hestenes phase axis $K = Jε$ acts as the imaginary unit for the 
split-octonionic proxy. 
In the block representation, $K$ is the canonical out-of-diagonal axis 
$(\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix})$ that manages the phase sectors.

claiming the analytic construction of the functional determinant.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.SuperMetriplectic.relativeModularSupervolume_secondVariation_is_sinkhornPerelmanKreinMetric

the second variation of the relative modular supervolume potential is exactly
the symmetric Krein Hessian bilinear form used by the Sinkhorn/Perelman metric
lane.

This theorem is a SuperMetriplectic-facing alias of the owner theorem in
`RelativeModularBerezinianBridge`; no Type III trace-density Taylor series is
postulated here.

The field `zornTotal_eq_bodyFisher` states that the Zorn body total is the same
observable Fisher quadratic.  This keeps the `STr` signed readout separate from
the physically ordered body quantity.

declarations.name: InfoGeometry.SuperMetriplectic.ZornSupertraceFisherBridge.zorn_total_nonnegative

the body quantity is nonnegative, while the raw supertrace remains the signed
even-minus-odd readout.
